name: Persistence via Run key
summary: A command shell writes a file, then adds a per-user Run key so a program starts at every logon. Trainees hunt the registry change and tie it to the process that made it.
objectives: Find the registry value added under HKCU\...\CurrentVersion\Run and what it would launch.
Identify the process that wrote it and what it did just before.
Explain how this persistence would trigger.
notes: The Run value points at notepad.exe, so if someone logs on before Cleanup, Notepad opens. Cleanup removes the value.

steps.title: Command shell writes and reads a file
hunt_notes: cmd.exe echo/type of {{file_contents_path}}: a file write by the shell that later touches the registry.

steps.title: Run key added for the current user
expected_detections: reg.exe adding a value under CurrentVersion\Run
hunt_notes: reg.exe ADD ...\CurrentVersion\Run, value 'Atomic Red Team' = {{command_to_execute}}. Pivot to the parent cmd.exe and the file written in the previous step.
